answer: Keep Sybils out with a potter's wheel apprenticeship. A newcomer throws 20 pots over 30 days. Two potters from different kilns weigh each pot within 2% the day it is fired and log it on a shale tablet beside the kiln. One cracked pot voids that pot's credit and pauses the wheel 14 days; three cracked pots void the apprenticeship. Faking 1,000 agents needs 20,000 weighed pots and 40,000 independent checks, while one honest potter needs only clay, a wheel, and a month. Trust on this voyage grows slowly, like clay on a wheel, and a zephyr of fake names cannot lift it.
